headline: Nvidia RTX 5090 GPUs worth $470,000 vanish from Brazilian airport
summary: A Brazilian distributor is seeking answers after two pallets of high-end graphics cards disappeared from Guarulhos International Airport, marking an unprecedented loss in its 38-year history.
details: A Brazilian IT distributor, Oderço, has taken to Instagram to report the disappearance of a shipment of Nvidia RTX 5090 GPUs valued at approximately $470,000 (R$2,500,000). The company stated this is the first such incident in its 38-year operational history.

The GPUs were expected to arrive at Guarulhos International Airport in São Paulo, but after reaching the airport, the two pallets reportedly vanished. Oderço claims it has not received any official explanation or response regarding its inquiries about the missing shipment.

The RTX 5090 is currently in extremely short supply globally, with many retailers listing it as unavailable. This disappearance exacerbates the difficulty in acquiring the top-tier gaming GPU, especially given its high acquisition cost for distributors.

While the exact number of missing GPUs is not specified, the distributor's stated acquisition cost suggests a significant quantity. For context, individual Zotac Gaming GeForce RTX 5090 cards are priced around $8,000 on Amazon and R$33,999.99 on Brazilian retailer Promotech, indicating a potential loss of at least 63 units at minimum.
This incident follows a pattern of high-value hardware theft, including previous cases of GPU shipments being stolen during delivery or even elaborate heists targeting AI hardware shipments.

headline_marked: [[DLSS 5]] modded into unsupported games shows up to 90% performance boost
headline: DLSS 5 modded into unsupported games shows up to 90% performance boost
summary: Modders have extracted Nvidia's latest DLSS 5 Neural Rendering model and are testing it on older titles, revealing substantial performance gains over previous versions.
details: A new version of Nvidia's DLSS 5 Neural Rendering (NR) model has been released, and the modding community has already extracted it to run in unsupported games. Early comparisons show performance improvements of up to 90% in titles like The Witcher 3 when compared to the older NR model.

To achieve these gains, Nvidia has made the AI model 24% smaller and it uses 20% less VRAM at 4K. This increased efficiency allows the neural rendering workload to be processed up to twice as fast, a crucial development given the limitations of consumer GPU VRAM.

The latest DLSS 5 DLL includes both the older and newer models as presets, simplifying performance comparisons. Modders are injecting the DLSS NR model into games using tools like RenoDX or OptiScaler, allowing for fine-tuning of settings.

While Nvidia plans to officially release DLSS 5 for RTX 40-series GPUs, the modding community has already modified the runtime to support older RTX 20-series cards, expanding its accessibility beyond official support.
These community efforts highlight the potential of DLSS 5 and the ongoing innovation in AI-driven graphics enhancement, even on hardware that doesn't meet the official requirements.
